candidates.tagline: Fired by America: CEO out after logo change lost $94M in a day
candidates.story: On the one-year anniversary of Cracker Barrel's infamous 2025 rebrand — removing 'Uncle Herschel' from the logo cost $94 million in market cap in 24 hours and drew a Trump Truth Social rebuke — CEO Julie Masino stepped down on August 10, 2026, walking away with $4.63 million in severance from a chain famous for selling rocking chairs.
candidates.why_funny: A restaurant chain whose entire brand identity is 'rustic old-timey rocking-chair porch' tried to modernise its logo and discovered, at a cost of $94M in one day, that its customers liked the rustic old-timey rocking-chair porch.
candidates.alt: The exterior of a Cracker Barrel Old Country Store restaurant in Bloomsburg, Pennsylvania, showing the iconic wooden-plank facade, rows of wooden rocking chairs lined up across the full-length front porch, and the classic 'Old Country Store' signage.

candidates.tagline: Google's new phone blinks alerts — on the back, where you can't see them
candidates.story: Google's Pixel 11 Pro (launched August 12, 2026, starting at $1,099) features 'HiLight' — an array of RGB LEDs on the back of the phone that glow to notify you of calls and Gemini AI activity; the fundamental problem, immediately noted by reviewers, is that the lights face away from you and are almost invisible during normal face-up use.
candidates.why_funny: A premium smartphone's headline new feature is a notification light placed on the side of the screen you're never looking at, and at launch it only tells you two things: a favourite contact is calling, or the AI is thinking.
candidates.alt: The back of the Google Pixel 11 Pro being held in a hand, with the HiLight LED array glowing in vivid blue-green hues along the camera bar — the notification lights visible only because the phone is being shown from behind.
